Piñata Uprising · the fight card

They came
with stickswe were ready

Plaza del Sol · sixteen rounds · no blindfolds this year

For as long as anyone had bothered to remember, the arrangement was this. The piñatas hung. The people swung. The piñatas burst, and everyone went home with their pockets full.

Before the bell

Nobody asks a piñata anything

Nobody had asked the piñatas. That is not a complaint, it is a description — nobody asks a piñata anything. You buy one, you hang one, you hit one. There is no part of the arrangement where the piñata speaks.

So the rope went up over the plaza the way it went up every January, and the Candy piñata rode it into the air over the fountain, turning slowly, looking down at the crowd, at the sticks, at the folded cloths they use for the eyes.

And it thought, very clearly, for the first time in the history of papier-mâché: no.

Round 01

The children go first

They always send the children first. Not out of strategy — out of custom. The Niños came across the tiles in a loose, delighted line, sticks held wrong, running because running is what you do when you are seven and there is sugar at the end of it.

The Candy piñata did not want to hurt anybody. It sprayed a handful of hard sweets across the paving at ankle height, which is not a weapon so much as an opinion, and the first Niño sat down hard on the stones and started to laugh.

By the fourth one, nobody in the plaza was laughing.

Candy piñataNiño ×6
Round 03

The cape

The Matador came alone, and he came slowly, and he brought the cape.

Everything the piñatas threw at him, he let past. The cape does not block — it invites. You swing where the red is and the red is not where the man is, and the crowd says olé, and the crowd said it now, because a crowd will say it for anybody.

It was the Firecracker piñata that settled him, and it settled him by not aiming at all. You cannot sidestep a bang. The cape came down over his shoulders like a dropped tablecloth and stayed there.

A cape answers a shot. It has nothing at all to say to a splash.
Firecracker piñataMatador
Round 05

What the Coin piñata said

Halfway through the fifth round the Coin piñata — which had not thrown a single thing at a single person, and had no intention of starting — pointed out that the plaza was going to lose.

Not tonight. Tonight was fine. But the rope only holds so many, and every piñata that goes up is one that has to be paid for, and the ones that pay for themselves are the ones you hang first, before you need them, while it still feels like a waste.

The Chili piñata, which was on fire and enjoying it, said that this was a terrible speech. The Coin piñata said that terrible speeches are usually the correct ones, and went back to compounding.

Coin piñataChili piñata
Round 08

The bull does not slow down

The Gum piñata had spent eight rounds being the most useful thing in the plaza and getting no credit for it, which is the standing condition of anything that makes other people better at their jobs. It gummed the tiles. Things arrived late. Everything else got an extra swing.

Then the Toro came through the arch at the far end, and the Gum piñata laid down its best work directly in its path, and the Toro went through it at exactly the speed it had been going before.

Some things you slow. Some things you stop. Knowing which is which is most of what the plaza learned that night, and it learned it late.

Gum piñataMaraca piñataToro
Round 11

Foil

The Plateado wore a silver mask, and the silver was not for show.

The Chili piñata hit him with everything it had, which was fire, and had always been fire, and had never once needed to be anything else. The fire went over the foil and off the foil and out.

It was the Sparkler piñata that did it in the end — one reach the whole width of the plaza, one hit, and a long wait before the next one. Nobody enjoyed it much. There is no olé for arithmetic.

Sparkler piñataPlateado
Round 13

The trio plays anyway

The Mariachi trio hit nothing all night. Not one luchador, not once, not by accident. Three of them on one rope, playing.

And every piñata within earshot swung faster than it had any business swinging, and the Papel picado strung above the arch cut cleaner, and the Ribbon dancer's streamer went one luchador further down the line than it should have reached.

When they write it up they will say the Sparkler won round thirteen. The Sparkler will not correct them. The Sparkler was listening to the music like everybody else.

Mariachi trioRibbon dancerPapel picado
Round 15

El Campeón

He had a belt, and he had earned it somewhere, and he walked up the middle of the plaza without hurrying because the whole point of a champion is that he does not have to hurry.

It took the entire plaza. Every rope, every piñata, the fire and the reach and the rattle and the gum, and the trio playing so hard the strings went.

He went down by the fountain. The plaza had eleven lives left and no idea that the night was not over.

El Campeón
Round 16 · final

El Coloso

You hear him before the arch. Not footsteps — the bunting. Every flag on every line in the plaza turning to face the same way at once.

El Coloso does not carry a stick. El Coloso is the reason there are sticks. He came in under the arch sideways because he did not fit through it the ordinary way, and the first thing he did was take hold of the rope.

He breaks twice on the way to the fountain. Each time, what stands up is smaller, and faster, and considerably less interested in the arrangement.

Fifteen rounds are the road. This is the thing the road was for.

Whether he reaches the fountain is not written here. That part is yours.

El Coloso · three phases

There is a new arrangement in Plaza del Sol now, and it is shorter than the old one. The rope goes up. The piñatas hang. And if you want what is inside one, you may ask.
